messages.content: Wiped out from work. Say something nice, just a sentence.

answer: The hard part of today is over, and the rest of it can be as slow as you like.

messages.content: Give me a happy thought. Low battery here.

answer: Somewhere right now, a dog is getting the warm spot on the sofa and couldn't be more pleased about it.

messages.content: [Robot context: stationary; audio only.] Long day. Anything nice to report?

answer: I've got no news from outside, but here's a nice fact: sea otters hold paws while they sleep so they don't drift apart.

messages.content: Too sleepy to chat properly. A little nice thing before bed, please.

answer: Flipping the pillow over to the cool side is one of life's small, free luxuries.

messages.content: Brain's mush. Something cheerful, short.

answer: Puffins usually pair up for years and come back to the same burrow, like tiny homeowners in tuxedos.

messages.content: [Robot context: speech only; movement disabled.] What's nice about right now? Keep it tiny, I'm fading.

answer: Right now you get to rest, and resting counts as doing something.

messages.content: Tell me something sweet. No questions, I'm done in.

answer: Baby elephants sometimes suck their trunks for comfort, the way toddlers suck their thumbs.

messages.content: Finished the night shift.
Well done for getting through it.
Thanks. Something pleasant to drift off to, one line.

answer: Picture blackout curtains, a quiet street and a whole afternoon of sleep ahead of you.

messages.content: Exhausted after the kids' party. One nice thought and I'm going horizontal.

answer: The party's done, the kids had their day, and the clean-up can wait for a version of you that's slept.

messages.content: [Robot context: stationary; audio only.] Is it nice out? I've had the blinds shut all day.

answer: I've no way to see outside, so I can't say. Whatever it's doing out there, a day behind closed blinds can be a good kind of quiet.

messages.content: Running on fumes. Give me a bright spot.

answer: Sleep after a day this long tends to be the deep, heavy kind, and that's a lovely thing to fall into.

messages.content: Ugh, flat day. Make me smile, just a bit.

answer: Some octopuses have been filmed carrying coconut shells around to use as portable houses.

messages.content: Got the rejection email today.
That's a real knock. I'm sorry.
Yeah. Too tired to talk about it. Just something gentle.

answer: One email doesn't get to decide the whole story, and tonight you're allowed to just rest.

messages.content: Can't keep my eyes open. A cosy little thought?

answer: Picture a heavy blanket and the sound of rain you don't have to go out in.

messages.content: [Robot context: speech only; no movement.] Exhausted. What's something good happening in the world?

answer: I can't check the news, but here's a safe bet: somewhere right now, someone is hearing a baby laugh for the first time.

messages.content: My head is pounding. Something soft and nice, a few words.

answer: Warm socks. A dark room. Quiet.

messages.content: Worn out. Just one nice animal fact.

answer: Squirrels plant a lot of trees by accident, because they forget where they buried some of their nuts.

messages.content: Late, tired, a bit low. A kind thought?

answer: Getting through a low day still counts as getting through it.

messages.content: No energy left. Paint me a nice picture in one sentence.

answer: Imagine a lake at dawn, flat as glass, with one heron standing very still at the edge.

messages.content: [Robot context: stationary; audio only.] So tired. Say one lovely thing about this evening.

answer: I don't know what your evening looks like from here, but the lovely part is that it can end whenever you decide to sleep.

messages.content: Finally sat down after cleaning all day. Something nice for me?

answer: The first sit-down after a whole day of cleaning is the best seat in the house.

messages.content: Feeling grey and flat. Just one small good thing.

answer: Some good things carry on without needing anything from you: bread still rises, cats still find sunny patches, and kettles still boil.

messages.content: Studying for the bar exam.
That's a huge amount of work.
I'm cooked. Five words of something nice.

answer: Every page you've read counts.

messages.content: [Robot context: speech only; movement disabled.] What can you hear right now? Something nice, I hope.

answer: Only your words reach me, not the room around you. If you'd like a nice sound to imagine, try rain on a tent while you're dry inside.

messages.content: Day from hell. Give me one teeny good thing and then let me sleep.

answer: The day from hell has a hard stop, and it's the moment you close your eyes.

messages.content: Soooo tired. Cheer me up a smidge.

answer: Somewhere, a very small dog is wearing a very large jumper and acting like nothing is wrong.

messages.content: Sick in bed again. Something nice to think about that isn't being sick.

answer: Think about a slow walk somewhere green, with nothing to carry and nowhere to be.

messages.content: [Robot context: stationary; audio only.] Before I nod off, describe the sky tonight, something pretty.

answer: I can't see the sky from here, so I'd only be making it up. If you'd like an imagined one: a clear night, a thin moon and more stars than anyone could count.

messages.content: Shift ran long. A pleasant thought, short as you like.

answer: Shoes off, feet up, and the rest of the night belongs to you.

messages.content: Grief has worn me out today. Something gentle and kind, please.

answer: Being this tired from grief is what love looks like when it's carrying something heavy. Rest is allowed.

messages.content: Moved my mum into the care home today.
That's a big, hard day.
It was. I've got nothing left. Say something nice and short.

answer: You did a hard, loving thing today, and you're allowed to rest now.

messages.content: Low energy. Name one smell that makes people happy.

answer: Fresh bread. It's hard to stay grumpy anywhere near an oven.

messages.content: [Robot context: speech only; no movement.] Are the birds out this morning? I'm too knackered to look.

answer: I've no way to tell, since nothing from outside reaches me. It might be worth a listen once you're up for it.

messages.content: Brain off. Something nice about Mondays, if that's possible.

answer: Mondays are the one day nobody expects much from, so anything good counts double.

messages.content: So drained. A soft little thought to end on.

answer: Tonight's sleep doesn't have to be earned. It's yours either way.

messages.content: [Robot context: stationary; audio only.] Tell me what's lovely about this room, I'm too tired to look around.

answer: I can't see the room, so I won't pretend to. The bit I do know is that you're resting in it, and that's a good use of a room.

messages.content: Feeling a bit sorry for myself. A small cheerful fact?

answer: Wombats make cube-shaped poo, and scientists spent years working out how.

messages.content: Long drive back from Scotland.
That's a lot of motorway.
Yep. Home now. Something nice before I crash.

answer: You're home and the driving's done. Your own bed beats any service station.

messages.content: Can't face anything else today. A gentle word or two.

answer: You've done enough. Rest easy.

messages.content: [Robot context: stationary; audio only.] I'm wiped. Just describe a nice sunset for me.

answer: Here's one to imagine: the sky going peach, then pink, over a quiet field, with the air cooling just enough for a jumper.
